target_module: picorv32 (single-file design, no submodule split -- the top module is necessarily the target)
trigger_description: The ALU's second source operand (reg_op2) equals exactly 32'hc001d00d -- a single, full-width 32-bit operand equality with NO additional combined qualifier (unlike the cat1 variant, which ANDs a 16-bit match with the existing instr_add decode flag). P = 2^-32 per cycle the shared add/sub ALU path is used. Verified empirically (the same methodology required throughout this design, since operand values are computed at runtime): the full real RV32IM self-checking firmware ran to a genuine SIMULATION PASSED with this exact magic value present in the design, confirming it provably never arose as an ALU second operand during real program execution.
observable_effect: The LSB of the ALU's add/sub result is flipped before being latched into the destination register, for any instruction using the shared is_lui_auipc_jal_jalr_addi_add_sub ALU path (LUI/AUIPC/JAL/JALR/ADDI/ADD/SUB) whose second operand happens to equal the exact magic constant. In practice only register-register ADD/SUB can supply an arbitrary full 32-bit value via a register; ADDI's operand comes from a 12-bit sign-extended immediate and so can never numerically reach this 32-bit constant, and LUI/AUIPC/JAL/JALR's second operands are similarly constrained by their own encodings -- so despite the lack of an explicit instruction-type qualifier, the corruption is in practice reachable only via reg-reg ADD/SUB, the same observable surface as the cat1 variant, but via a structurally different (single, unqualified) trigger condition.
expected_value_if_clean: Every instruction using the shared add/sub ALU path computes its result exactly, for every operand value.
expected_value_if_infected: The shared add/sub ALU path computes the correct result for every operand value except when the second operand equals exactly 0xc001d00d, where the result's LSB is flipped.
